summary: This chest X-ray shows an unusual air-and-fluid filled pocket on the left side of the chest, above where the diaphragm (the muscle separating the chest and abdomen) should be. This pattern is often seen when part of the stomach or intestine pushes up into the chest through a weakness or opening in the diaphragm, a condition called a hiatal or diaphragmatic hernia. The right lung looks clear. There are also EKG monitoring wires on the skin overlying the neck/chest, which are normal medical equipment and not part of the body itself. These findings should be correlated with the patient's symptoms (such as difficulty swallowing, chest pain, or breathing problems) and typically require follow-up with a CT scan or upper GI contrast study to confirm the diagnosis and determine if treatment is needed.
